names: la: principium influens esse in aliud
la: id ad cujus esse aliquid sequitur

answers.label: That upon whose being the being of another follows: a principle that flows being into another

questions.wording: How many kinds of cause are there?

answers.label: Four: matter, form, the efficient cause and the end

questions.wording: What is the nature of a natural thing, in the sense natural philosophy uses?

answers.label: The principle and cause of motion and rest in that in which it is, first and by itself (Aristotle's definition)
The internal cause by which a natural body has its essence, properties, actions and passions

questions.wording: Does nature act for an end?

answers.label: Yes
No: nature's works come about by chance or by the necessity of matter

questions.wording: Was the world made for man's sake?
names: la: totum universum hominis causa conditum

answers.label: Yes: the whole world with its parts serves man's use
No

questions.wording: Do created things truly act and produce effects, or is God the only efficient cause?

answers.label: Created things truly act, as second causes under God
God alone is properly the efficient cause; bodies cannot move themselves or one another

questions.wording: When God works wonders in nature, does he act against nature?

answers.label: No: miracles are above nature, not against it, since creatures obey their creator
God can act against a thing's natural inclination and do it violence

questions.wording: Can art make the things that nature makes?

answers.label: No: art makes only accidents; nature makes substances
Some, by applying natural active powers to fit matter, but not those whose producing powers are beyond art
Causes by accident, from which an effect follows beyond the agent's intention: fortune in agents acting by choice, chance in natural agents

questions.wording: Does anything happen by fortune or chance with respect to God?

answers.label: No: nothing is fortuitous to God, who foresees and orders everything
Yes

questions.wording: Is there a fate, and what is it?

answers.label: Yes, rightly understood: an order of events and causes foreknown and preordained by God
An absolute necessity of all things from the linking of causes, binding even God
An inevitable impression of the stars to which everything is subject
No: the world is not ruled by any providence, and everything happens by chance

questions.wording: Does fate, or God's foreknowledge, lay necessity on the human will?

answers.label: No
Yes

questions.wording: Do the heavens govern the coming to be, passing away and lasting of things below the moon?

answers.label: Yes: the heavenly bodies flow into the generation, corruption and duration of things below
No

questions.wording: Do the stars govern the human will?

answers.label: No
Yes
An error or defect of nature, which fails of the end it aims at through some fault in a cause

questions.wording: Is a monster judged against the right form of its kind alone, or against what is right and usual?
names: la: a recta et solita dispositione degenerans

answers.label: Against the right form alone: what is a monster in one place is a monster everywhere
Against the right and usual disposition of the kind

questions.wording: Are the offspring of two different kinds, such as the mule, monsters?

answers.label: Yes
No

questions.wording: Can a true human being be begotten of a human and a beast?

answers.label: No
Yes
